doc.headline: No configuration clears both gates as measured: every one that holds the pass-rate gate misses the latency budget overall, and every one inside the latency budget misses pass rate somewhere.
doc.lede: Brisk-S with high reasoning and one retry passes in every task at {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.mean}, but its p95 is {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} against {criteria.p95.threshold}. Per-task latency figures would change this only if they were held.

caveats.material_if: a claim says one arm beats another; no arm is read paired, so arms compare only by their own figures and intervals.
the near-miss arm is picked: the best of {n_candidates} configurations reads high by chance, so a re-run would tend to read it lower.

decision.text: The gates are read per task, but latency is held only over all cases, so no arm has a per-task latency figure. Two arms pass pass rate in every task and miss p95 overall; the other sixteen miss pass rate in at least one task.

Atlas-M with high reasoning and one retry has p95 of {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.high.r1.p95} and costs {measure.cost_per_1k.atlas-m.high.r1.mean} per 1k calls. Brisk-S low reasoning with one retry costs {measure.cost_per_1k.brisk-s.low.r1.mean}, is inside the budget overall at {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95}, and misses pass rate by {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.multihop.gap} points in multi-hop and {criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.disamb.gap} in ambiguous entity.
Declare whether the latency gate applies to each task or to all calls together, and hold per-task p95. Then decide whether a miss of under two points on the nearest arm is acceptable.
Run Brisk-S with low reasoning and one retry again on more cases, with per-task latency held, to see whether it reaches the pass-rate gate in multi-hop and ambiguous entity.

claims.text: No arm clears every gate: sixteen miss the {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} pass-rate gate in at least one task, and the two that clear it everywhere are not shown to meet the latency budget.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task for the five arms that come nearest the gate; Brisk-S high with retry and Atlas-M high with retry clear it in every task.

claims.text: Latency is what removes the two arms that pass quality: Brisk-S high with retry runs at {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.high.r1.p95} and Atlas-M high with retry at {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.high.r1.p95}, both over the {criteria.p95.threshold} budget.

evidence.caption: Median to p95 latency for all arms against the budget; this is over all cases, not per task.

claims.text: A retry is the cheapest way to buy pass rate: for Brisk-S at low reasoning it lifts the rate from {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r0.mean} to {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean} for {measure.cost_per_1k.brisk-s.low.r1.mean} against {measure.cost_per_1k.brisk-s.low.r0.mean} per 1k calls.

evidence.caption: Cost per 1k calls (log axis) against overall pass rate for all eighteen arms; Nano-XS is cheapest and furthest below the gate.

explore.control: The latency gate's scope (each task or all calls)
explore.binds: Whether any arm can be called a survivor
explore.outcome: Read over all calls, Brisk-S low with retry is inside at {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95}; read per task it has no figure.

omitted.why: All six miss pass rate in every task; they do not change the call.

omitted.what: Per-arm gate gaps for the other arms
omitted.why: Held in the options table; they add nothing to the reading.

next.text: Hold per-task p95 for the Brisk-S and Atlas-M arms with high reasoning.
next.settles: Whether either high-reasoning arm with retry meets the latency gate in every task.

next.text: Re-run Brisk-S low with retry on more cases.
next.settles: Whether its multi-hop and ambiguous-entity misses are real or noise.

method.text: A trial passes by the campaign's own definition; none is stated in the snapshot, so it is not described here.
Pass rate at least {criteria.pass_rate.threshold} and p95 at most {criteria.p95.threshold}, each read in every task.
Per-task pass rates state no interval, so near misses cannot be called borderline or missed.
Cost per 1k calls as measured; the provider routing is not named for any arm. Volume is {meta.volume_per_month} a month.
